scenarios.title: The First Big Purchase
scenarios.text: You can finally afford the car you've wanted since you were fifteen, the one on the poster above your childhood bed. The dealer already knows your name when you walk in.

choices.label: Buy it and drive it home
choices.result: Bought, and driven straight home to {parent}'s driveway. He walks around it three times without speaking, then asks for the keys.

choices.label: Buy something sensible
choices.result: Something sensible, with good mileage, and the rest goes in the bank. It's a good car. It isn't the car, and you notice every time you see one.

choices.label: Wait one more year
choices.result: A year's wait, on purpose. The wanting fades a little, and so does the fun of it, and you're not sure whether that's wisdom or a loss.

scenarios.title: The Regional Endorsement
scenarios.text: A regional grocery chain offers you a sponsorship worth more than your whole rookie salary: commercials, store openings, your face on cereal boxes in three states.

choices.label: Sign the deal
choices.result: Signed. The shoots take some weekends, the money is real, and {sibling} buys forty boxes of cereal with your face on them.

choices.label: Strike two clauses first
choices.result: The fine print, read twice, and two clauses struck: no appearances in season, no exclusivity. They agree, and you keep your Tuesdays.

choices.label: Keep your weekends
choices.result: A pass, and your weekends stay yours. A rival kicker takes the deal, and you see his face in every aisle for a year.

scenarios.title: The Investment Pitch
scenarios.text: A man at a charity dinner pitches you an investment: guaranteed returns, a famous partner, no risk. He's done this before, and he knows you can tell.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.result: You thank him and walk away. Six months later you read his name in the paper, and you pass the article to your teammates.

choices.label: Ask someone you trust
choices.result: You show it to someone you trust. They laugh, then explain exactly how it works. You learn more in an hour than in a year of statements.

choices.label: Put money in
choices.result: You put money in. The statements look great for a while, then they stop coming, and so does he. The shame lasts longer than the loss.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Mentor
scenarios.text: The club asks you to help a younger player adjust: a nervous second-year punter who eats lunch alone and calls home after every practice. Someone once did this for you.

choices.label: Take the punter on
choices.result: Meals, film, the long drives home: all of it, on your shoulders for a season. He's steadier by midseason and starts eating lunch at the specialists' table.

choices.label: Be a friend, not a mentor
choices.result: Friendly instead of formal: video games, bad movies, no lectures. He calls you when it really matters, and it does, twice.

choices.label: Point him to a veteran
choices.result: A veteran with more time and more patience gets the job, at your suggestion. It works out fine, and you feel a small pang at the specialists' table.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Reputation
scenarios.text: Younger teammates have started looking at you when something goes wrong: a bad practice, a fight in the weight room, a rumor about a trade. You're not sure when you became that person.

choices.label: Step into it
choices.result: You step into it. When the room gets loud, you're the calm voice, and by December the coaches start running things past you first.

choices.label: Pick your moments
choices.result: Rare words, carefully chosen. You speak up twice all season, in two bad weeks, and both times the room listens completely.

choices.label: Stay a kicker
choices.result: There are captains for that, you decide, and you stay a kicker. The young players find someone else, and you're relieved and a little sorry.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Change
scenarios.text: A new special teams coach arrives with a new way of doing everything: new drills, new warmups, a new word for every old thing. He's thirty-four and very confident.

choices.label: Try every new drill
choices.result: Every new drill, without complaint, for a month. Some of it actually helps, and he notices who didn't fight him.

choices.label: Keep what works
choices.result: What works, kept; what doesn't, explained calmly. He respects the reasoning, argues once, and then adopts one of your drills.

choices.label: Get to know him first
choices.result: Lunch, his story, his family, before you judge a single drill. He turns out to be nervous, and the drills make more sense after that.

scenarios.title: The Public Relationship
scenarios.text: Your relationship becomes a topic of public interest after a photo goes around, and {love_interest} didn't sign up for that. There are strangers in the comments of their private account.

choices.label: Protect {love_interest}
choices.result: Nothing about home, posted ever again, not even a photo of the dog. {love_interest} notices, and is quietly grateful, and the strangers lose interest by spring.

choices.label: Set boundaries together
choices.result: What stays private and what doesn't: decided together, at the kitchen table, with a list. It feels like a team, which it is.

choices.label: Let it blow over
choices.result: It'll blow over, you decide. It takes much longer than you thought, and {love_interest} deletes the account without telling you.

scenarios.title: The First Home Repair
scenarios.text: The roof leaks the week of a road trip, all over the living room, and the repair estimate is the size of a used car. You're in a hotel two thousand miles away.

choices.label: Handle it from the hotel
choices.result: Contractors, insurance and photos, all handled by phone from the hotel. It gets done, expensively, and you miss a meeting doing it.

choices.label: Ask {parent} to oversee it
choices.result: {parent} drives over with a ladder and an opinion, and oversees the whole repair. He loves being useful, and the roof is perfect.

choices.label: Patch it for now
choices.result: A tarp and a bucket for now, the real fix in the offseason. It's cheap, and you sleep under the sound of dripping all winter.

scenarios.title: The Charity Commitment
scenarios.text: A children's literacy nonprofit asks you to become a regular supporter: not a photo at the gala, but monthly visits, a reading program, and your name on a library wing.

choices.label: Commit to monthly visits
choices.result: Monthly visits, all year. The kids know your name by spring, and one of them reads you a whole book about a dragon who kicks.

choices.label: Bring teammates along
choices.result: Teammates, signed up one by one. It becomes a team tradition, and {holder} turns out to be the best reader of all of you.

choices.label: Write a check
choices.result: A generous check and a warm letter. It helps, and the director thanks you sincerely, and you never see the library wing.

scenarios.title: The Radio Segment
scenarios.text: A sports radio station offers you a recurring weekly segment: Monday mornings, fifteen minutes, live, with a host who likes to ask about locker-room drama.

choices.label: Take the segment
choices.result: Yes, every Monday at seven. You're good at it, the callers love you, and your Mondays disappear for the whole season into a radio booth.

choices.label: Try it for a month
choices.result: A one-month trial, then a decision. You keep it, shorter, with a promise from the host to leave the locker room alone.

choices.label: Keep your Mondays
choices.result: No segment. You'd rather talk about kicking with other kickers, and your Monday mornings stay quiet, slow and entirely yours.

scenarios.title: The Offseason Vacation
scenarios.text: {love_interest} wants a real vacation this offseason: two weeks, an island, no phones. You want to train. The brochure has been on the kitchen counter for a month, open to the same page.

choices.label: Go, and leave the ball home
choices.result: Two weeks on the island, no ball, no film, no phone. It's the best fortnight of the year, and you come back rested and in love all over again.

choices.label: Stay and train
choices.result: Training, alone, while {love_interest} goes with friends and sends pictures of the water every day. You're stronger by July and a little lonelier.

choices.label: Find an island with a field
choices.result: A beach town with a high school field, found after two hours of searching. Mornings for kicking, afternoons for the beach. Everyone wins, sort of.

scenarios.title: The Former Teammate
scenarios.text: A former teammate can't find another job in the league and keeps calling: late at night, after he's watched your games, asking if you've heard anything from anyone.

choices.label: Keep picking up
choices.result: Every call, picked up. Mostly he needs someone to listen, and some nights you stay on the phone until he's laughing again.

choices.label: Help him find other work
choices.result: Calls to people you know about jobs outside football: coaching, sales, broadcasting. One of them works out, and he sends you a photo from his new desk.

choices.label: Let some calls go
choices.result: Some calls go to voicemail. You feel bad about it every time, and you call back on Sundays, which helps a little.

scenarios.title: The New Neighborhood
scenarios.text: You've lived on this street for two years and know nobody's name. There's a block party flyer on your door and a kid next door who kicks a ball against your garage every afternoon.

choices.label: Go to the block party
choices.result: The block party, with a casserole you bought. By the end of the night you know every name on the street, and the neighbors start bringing food after losses.

choices.label: Help with the youth league
choices.result: The neighborhood youth league gets a volunteer coach once a week. The kid next door is on your team, and he's terrible, and you love it.

choices.label: Keep to yourself
choices.result: You keep to yourself. It's quiet and private, and a little lonely when the street fills with music on Saturday nights.
